summary: Albert Grünwedel was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and archaeologist. He earned his doctorate at the University of Munich (1876–1883) under numerous scholars, later serving at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin (1881–1921; director from 1904) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1891).

Albert Hoefer worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Greifswald, Göttingen, and Berlin, where he completed his doctorate (1837) and habilitation (1838–1840). He spent his career as a professor at the University of Greifswald (~1840–1883).
Albert Hofmann studied at the University of Zurich from around 1925 to 1929. He subsequently held a post at Novartis from approximately 1929 to 1971.

Albert Lutz is a scholar of Sinology and archaeology. He studied at the University of Zurich under Eberhard Fischer (~1974–1982) and had a long career at Museum Rietberg as curator for Chinese art (1982) and director (1998–2019).

Albert Schweitzer worked in philosophy and religious studies. He studied under Wilhelm Deecke and attended the universities of Strasbourg, Tübingen, and Prague. He later held a post at the University of Strasbourg from around 1902 to 1912.

Albert Sechehaye was a linguist who studied at the University of Geneva (~1889–1898), where he was a pupil of Ferdinand de Saussure (~1893–1903). He subsequently held a post at the University of Geneva from around 1903 to 1945.

Albert Thumb was a linguist who studied under Karl Brugmann, Hermann Osthoff, and Rudolf Thurneysen, completing his habilitation at the University of Freiburg (~1888–1891). He held posts at Freiburg (1891–1895), Marburg (~1901–1909), and Strasbourg (1909).

Albert Welter is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at McMaster University (~1980–1986) under Koichi Shinohara, Yün-hua Jan, and Ryosho Tanaka. He held posts at the University of Winnipeg (~1995–2013) and the University of Arizona (2013).
Alberto Todeschini is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He has held posts as a guest at Kyoto University and at the Italian School of East Asian Studies (attested 2010).

Albion Moonlight Butters is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Harvard, CIHTS, and Columbia University (PhD 2006) under numerous teachers and supervisors, including Robert A. F. Thurman, Noel Q. King, and Masatoshi Nagatomi.

Albrecht Hanisch is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Michael Hahn and earned a doctoral degree at the University of Marburg (2000). He held posts at the Nepal Research Centre and the Nepalese-German Manuscript Cataloguing Project.

Albrecht Weber was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Breslau, Bonn, and Berlin under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler, Christian Lassen, Johann Gildemeister, and Adalbert Kuhn. He held teaching posts at Humboldt University of Berlin from 1848 to 1901.

Albrecht Wezler was an Indologist and philosopher who completed his doctorate at the University of Tübingen (~1960–1965) under Paul Thieme. He served as a director at the University of Hamburg (1973–2003) and the Nepal Research Centre (1982–2004).

Aleix Ruiz-Falqués specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He completed his PhD at the University of Cambridge under Eivind Kahrs (2016) and has held posts at the Shan State Buddhist University, SUTD, and the Pali Text Society.

Aleksander Brückner was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at Lviv, Vienna, and Berlin under August Leskien, and subsequently held academic posts at the University of Lviv (~1878–1881) and Frederick William University Berlin (~1881–1924).
Alessandro Giudice is an Indologist who has held posts at the University of Munich and as a Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

Alessandro Graheli specializes in Indology and philosophy. He has held positions at the University of Vienna, the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia, and the University of Toronto as a Part-time Assistant Professor.

Alex McKay is a historian and Tibetologist who completed his PhD at SOAS University of London in 1995. He has held research fellowships at SOAS, University College London, and the International Institute for Asian Studies.

Alex Watson is an Indologist and philosopher educated at Oxford and SOAS, supervised by Alexis Sanderson and Harunaga Isaacson. He held posts at Wolfson College, Oxford, Harvard University as Preceptor in Sanskrit, and Ashoka University.

Alex Wayman was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. Educated at UCLA and UC Berkeley (PhD) under Ferdinand Lessing and Murray Barnson Emeneau, he taught at Berkeley, Michigan, Wisconsin-Madison (~1961–1967), and Columbia University (1967–1991).
